title: CSV parsing: RFC 4180 quoting and duplicate code or mapping rejection
scenario: 1) parseCsvRecords on quoted commas, doubled quotes, a newline in quotes, CRLF, LF, a lone CR and no trailing newline, checking each record's starting line. 2) readLookupCsv where code A sets enabled/startDate/endDate on two rows, maps the same source and source code twice, and the same code appears under two lookup types.
expected: 1) Fields unquoted correctly, embedded newlines kept, each record reports its start line, final record kept; lone CR currently ends a record (pins current behavior, owner may want different intent). 2) Two errors naming both lines each, no duplicated mapping in the draft; same code under two types stays two values without error.

title: Pure-function units: merge immutability, panel message validation, discovery shape
scenario: 1) Deep-freeze a stored lookup value, call mergeLookupValue appending a mapping, then reuse it for planWarnings and unknownSourceWarnings. 2) parseLookupValuesMessage/validateLookupValues with wrong types, unknown type, extra fields (rdmTenantId, lookupTypeName), padded strings, duplicate codes, a code with '/', and 101 codes. 3) extractRdmConfig on a physical configuration with messaging credentials and storage accounts, plus null, strings, missing rdmConfig, blank serviceUri and invalid rdmTenants entries.
expected: 1) No exception from frozen input; stored object deep-equals its snapshot; merged result is a separate copy with the new mapping. 2) Malformed messages return undefined, extra fields dropped, text trimmed, rule breaches give kind rejected listing every error, over 100 codes rejected. 3) Result has exactly serviceUri and rdmTenantIds with no leaked field; bad shapes give serviceUri undefined and an empty list without throwing; valid ids keep order.

title: Contracts: RDM request URLs, verbatim PUT body, and menu guard on RDM nodes
scenario: 1) Capture stub-fetch URLs for rdmTenantId, lookupTypeName and tenantId values containing '/', '..', '?' and spaces. 2) Call putRdmConfiguration with a body string of custom whitespace and key order. 3) Evaluate every reltio.deleteNode and reltio.renameNode menu condition against the RDM context values (reltio.rdm.group, reltio.rdm.root, folder and item values).
expected: 1) URLs follow /reltio/tenants/{id}, /configuration/{id}, /lookups/{id}/{type} with encodeURIComponent, no extra segment or query; real functions are exercised. 2) PUT to /configuration/{rdmTenantId}, Content-Type application/json, body byte-identical to the input, Authorization carries the token. 3) No L3 edit command matches an RDM value; RDM nodes stay in the reltio.rdm.* namespace (a stale code comment says RDM is read-only although Apply now PUTs; guard the namespace, not the comment).

title: Load into existing codes keeps stored values and skips conflicting mappings
scenario: 1) Stored code B has two mappings, version, enabled=true and an endDate; the CSV row adds a new SAP mapping and states enabled=false and another endDate; run a load against a stubbed service. 2) Stored B maps BvD code B to 'Business'; one CSV row says 'Biz' and another repeats an identical stored mapping; plan and load.
expected: 1) The POSTed B equals the fetched value with only the SAP mapping added; enabled, endDate, version and existing mappings untouched; a warning says stored values are kept. 2) Conflicting row skipped with a warning naming its line, stored 'Business' never overwritten, identical row counted as already present, nothing sent if nothing is appendable.

title: Load and write failures are reported accurately and readably
scenario: 1) Load 250 codes with the second chunk POST failing with HTTP 400, then a 401 that cannot be refreshed, then a failing re-fetch. 2) Stub POST and PUT responses with a Reltio error envelope, plain text, empty body, a body longer than MAX_ERROR_BODY_CHARS, and 401.
expected: 1) 400 case: added 100, not-stored 100, not-sent 50; 401 case stops with api-error 401; without a re-fetch sent codes are unconfirmed; no code is added unless a response or the re-fetch holds it. 2) Envelope gives 'HTTP <status>: <message> <detail>' without duplicates; empty body gives 'HTTP <status>.'; long body truncated with an ellipsis; 401 gives ReltioApiError 'Unauthorized (401)' with statusCode 401.

title: Manual: Apply and Get Configuration guard against drift and missing baselines
scenario: Manual (Tier C), in a dev host. 1) Apply RDM Configuration: remove the baseline and run; restore it, change the server copy and run; leave the server unchanged and choose Yes; also try with an unsaved editor and with no token. 2) Get Configuration: edit RDM/{id}/config.json or delete its baseline; choose Fetch anyway in one run and dismiss the modal in another.
expected: 1) No baseline gives an error and no PUT; a server change shows a modal and applies only after diff review and confirm; unchanged server asks once then PUTs the saved text; unsaved or tokenless runs stop before any request. 2) Modal lists the drifted file; a missing baseline counts as drifted; dismiss leaves the local file untouched; Fetch anyway overwrites it and refreshes the baseline.

title: Security: approval gate, path confinement, token secrecy and trusted RDM hosts
scenario: 1) handleLookupLoadRequest in plan mode, load mode with approve false, and load mode with CSV errors, counting postValues and approve calls. 2) csvFile/rdmConfigFile with '..', backslash '..\\', another-drive absolute path, a path outside the workspace, and another tenant's RDM/<id>/config.json. 3) Fail every RDM client function (400/401/500, network error) and run a bridge load with token 'SECRET-TOKEN'; search errors, result.json and logs. 4) Call the four service-URI functions with evil.example.com and a trusted host.
expected: 1) Plan: zero posts and prompts; cancelled: zero posts; CSV errors: invalid-csv, zero prompts and posts; only approve true allows a post. 2) Each returns failed/invalid-request with zero fetch or post calls; backslash and other-drive cases are new. 3) SECRET-TOKEN and the Authorization value appear nowhere; extend the bridge assertion to the client functions. 4) Untrusted host throws UntrustedHostError with zero fetch calls; trusted host receives the token only there (today only POST is asserted).

title: Relocation never overwrites and is idempotent; bridge accepts Windows path spellings
scenario: 1) relocateRdmTargets on an in-memory fs with legacy config and baseline, with the config destination taken, then the baseline destination taken (Windows-style Uri paths). 2) Run relocation twice; make the baseline rename throw after the config moved and rerun; put a failing tenant before a healthy one. 3) With a Windows-style workspace root, send csvFile and rdmConfigFile using backslashes, mixed separators and a different drive-letter case.
expected: 1) Tenant listed under conflicts, no rename called, both legacy files stay, rename always uses overwrite false. 2) Second run does nothing; mid-pair failure reports failed once, config at its new path, stray legacy baseline not moved on rerun (pins current behavior, owner may want different intent), healthy tenant still moves. 3) In-workspace paths resolve, config path matches rdmConfigUri despite case and separator differences, request reaches status planned.

title: Panel HTML is nonce-protected and the service URI cache stays per tenant and in memory
scenario: 1) Render the lookup values panel twice for data with <script>, quotes and markup in codes, sources and suggestions. 2) Remember URIs for two tenants in two environments, remember an empty string, clear the cache, and inspect rdmServiceCache source for fs, vscode or storage use.
expected: 1) Every script and style carries the CSP nonce, no inline handlers, markup escaped, script body has no interpolated data, nonce and render token differ per render. 2) Recall returns the right URI per environment and tenant only; empty URI not stored; clear empties the cache; no file or storage writes (the physical-config response holds credentials).

title: CSV size and row limits accept the boundary and reject one past it
scenario: Build a file with exactly 10000 data rows and one with 10001; call readLookupCsv with byteLength exactly 2 MB and 2 MB + 1.
expected: 10000 rows and 2 MB parse without a limit error; 10001 rows gives 'limit is 10000' and 2 MB + 1 gives 'larger than 2 MB'; neither case throws.

title: Manual: request file watcher debounces, retries half-written files, answers in order
scenario: In a dev host write request.json in several chunks, then write two requests 100 ms apart, then write invalid JSON.
expected: One result per settled request, in order, with no interleaving; a half-written file is retried once before invalid-request; result.json is valid JSON ending in a newline. Needs a real file watcher.
